_comment: Copy to the repo root as routing.json and edit. v1 files (no 'version' key, flat rules with match/pattern/dest) still load and are converted in memory.
_comment_default: Used when no rule matches. Destination paths must be absolute; an invalid config is a startup error, never a silent fallback.
_comment_lists: Plain data referenced by signals. Adding a scanlation site is appending one string here.
_comment_signals: Named predicates. Fields are 'source', 'title', or 'comicinfo.<AnyElement>'. Operators: equals, in, in_list, glob, glob_in_list, glob_tokens_in_list, contains_any. Combinators: any, all, not. A missing ComicInfo field makes a matcher false, never an error.
_comment_glob_tokens_in_list: glob_tokens_in_list is glob_in_list for fields that hold a comma-joined list rather than one value, such as Publisher and Imprint. It splits on commas only, trims each token, ignores empty tokens, and matches when any token matches any pattern in the named list -- so an anchored pattern like 'yen press*' still matches 'Gangan Wing,Yen Press'. Use glob_in_list for single-valued fields such as Web, where a URL may legitimately contain a comma.
_comment_rules: Evaluated top to bottom, first match wins, then 'default'. Each rule may declare "strength": "strong" or "weak" -- how much its match is worth when a caller samples several archives of one series and has to rank their decisions. Omitted means strong. Callers rank authoritative decisions (a manual override, or an existing series folder) above all evidence, then strong above weak. Strength is never inferred from a rule's name.
_comment_overrides: Manual fixes, checked before everything else. Use 'aliases' to merge titles that differ by translation or romanisation rather than by punctuation -- normalisation already handles case, spacing, punctuation and censorship markers, but cannot know that two different words mean the same series. Add 'dest' to pin a series to a library outright. An alias claimed by two overrides is a config error rather than a silent coin flip.

series_overrides.canonical: Some Series That Keeps Getting Misrouted

_comment_series_index: A series that already has a folder in one of these destinations keeps going there, so it never splits across libraries because one chapter arrived without usable metadata. Built once per scan pass, not per directory. ORDER IS PRECEDENCE: if a series somehow exists in two libraries the first listed wins, so put the library whose membership encodes a human decision first -- Comix membership is a deliberate adult determination and must outrank a metadata-derived origin signal. Do NOT list a library that is being retired or is known-misclassified until its contents have been migrated, or the index will pin them where they sit.
